story: A Martian meteorite is a rock that formed on Mars, was ejected from the planet by an impact event, and traversed interplanetary space before landing on Earth. By the early 1980s, it was obvious that the SNC group of meteorites were significantly different from other meteorite types, leading scientists to suggest an origin from a parent body like Mars. Direct evidence came in 1983 when trapped gases in the EET79001 shergottite closely resembled the Martian atmosphere. As of September 2020, 277 meteorites had been classified as Martian. These rocks include shergottites, nakhlites, chassignites, and ungrouped specimens like Allan Hills 84001, which famously sparked intense debate in 1996 when NASA researchers reported it might contain fossilized microbial life. Today, scientists continue studying these rare samples to unlock the volcanic and aqueous history of the Red Planet.
angle: Rocks from the surface of Mars routinely get blasted off into deep space by massive asteroid impacts and eventually land on Earth as meteorites.

claims.claim: Shergottites make up roughly three-quarters of all Martian meteorites.
In 1996, NASA researchers announced that ALH 84001 appeared to contain fossilized remains of tiny life-forms.
Scientific consensus largely attributed the structures in ALH 84001 to earthly contamination or inorganic mineral growth rather than Martian life.
The Martian meteorite NWA 7034, nicknamed Black Beauty, contains ten times the water content of other Mars meteorites found on Earth.
NWA 7034 was found in the Sahara Desert in 2011 and weighs approximately 320 grams.

disputed: Whether the structures inside ALH 84001 represent ancient Martian microfossils or earthly contamination/inorganic processes. A script should attribute the life claims as a 1996 announcement by NASA researchers that sparked intense scientific debate and skepticism.
